verdict.rationale: Bruno is offline-only and stores collections as plain-text Bru files in a folder on the user's filesystem, with no cloud sync or account, so the data is already local, readable and versionable in Git. A release note also shows Postman export, which offers a route out to another tool. However, the native format is Bruno's own Bru markup rather than a widely standardized format, and there is no documented 'export all data' capability covering environments, settings and docs. Missing for 10: documented full-data export in standard open formats (e.g. OpenAPI/Postman for all collections and environments), documentation of Postman export beyond a release-note line, and independent hands-on evidence of migrating away.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Bruno stores your collections directly in a folder on your filesystem. We use a plain text markup language, Bru, to save information about API requests.
Bruno is offline-only. There are no plans to add cloud-sync to Bruno, ever.
Collections live as plain text files on your filesystem, so you can version them with Git and review API changes like code.
add preserve scripts option for Postman import/export
saves API request collection files in simple, human-readable text files that are designed to be committed to a source control repo and easily shared
